Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All evaluable conclusions in the plan match results recorded in the documentation. Causality scores for different filtering tasks (Object Type: 0.863, Profession: 0.836, Nationality: 0.504, Landmark: 0.576, Rhyme: 0.041) match exactly between plan and paper. Ablation results (SelectOne: 22.5%, SelectOne-MCQ: 0.4%, SelectFirst: 13.1%, SelectLast: 9.22%, Counting: 89.80%, CheckPresence: 98.61%) match. Cross-task generalization patterns (>=70% for Select* tasks), key state causality (0.783), and dual filtering strategy results (46.09% vs 96.06%) all match documentation.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All 5 methodology steps from the plan are implemented: (1) Causal mediation analysis with activation patching is implemented in src/selection/optimization.py and notebook 103_patching_within_task.ipynb; (2) DCM with sparse binary masks for head selection in optimization code; (3) Generalization testing across languages (English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Thai), formats (single line, bulleted), and 6 filter-reduce tasks; (4) Ablation studies comparing filter heads with Function Vector, Concept Induction, and random heads in notebook 111_necessity.ipynb; (5) Dual filtering investigation (question-before vs after) in notebook 103.2_ques_before_vs_after.ipynb.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: Effect sizes are clearly non-trivial relative to baseline variability. Filter head causality of 0.863 represents 86.3% accuracy in predicting the correct target item after intervention (well above random ~20% baseline). Ablation causes 77-99% accuracy drops (22.5% vs 100% for SelectOne, 0.4% vs 100% for MCQ, etc.) compared to only 0-3% for random head ablation. Delta logit values of +8-9 points indicate strong causal effects. Cross-lingual causality of 0.775-0.951 shows robust generalization, not marginal effects.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices explicitly justified: DCM addresses single-head intervention weakness (Section 2.3 explains other heads and backup mechanisms can rectify single-head interventions). Query patching at last token justified as 'where the LM is required to produce its answer'. Averaging qsrc removes position bias (Section F). Comparison with Function Vector, Concept, and Induction heads provides baseline for filter head novelty (Table 4). Intermediate conclusions supported: key state semantics confirmed by 78.3% causality with combined query-key intervention; dual filtering confirmed by 50% accuracy difference between question placement conditions.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key experimental results report appropriate uncertainty measures. Key state experiment reports ΔLogit = 8.26 ± 3.35 (mean ± std). Training-free probe reports 0.81 ± 0.02 accuracy. Evaluation conducted on 512 examples per condition provides reasonable statistical power. While not all results include explicit p-values, the effect sizes are large enough (77-99% accuracy drops vs 0-3% for controls) that statistical significance is clearly implied. Section L acknowledges limitations including potential for slight score variation across trials.
